browser.gl: ANGLE (Google, Vulkan 1.3.0, SwiftShader Device (LLVM 10.0.0)) — CPU rasterizer, no GPU
browser.served_from: http://127.0.0.1:8123/ via the repository's own serve.ts

network.note: performance.getEntriesByType('resource') on the running page; every entry is same-origin and inside game/. No font, image, audio or CDN fetch exists.

real_input_checks.observed: state playing, depth reset to 0, HUD shown, title overlay hidden
yaw 0 → 1.333 rad (1.6 rad/s); D 0.8 s brought it back to 0.053
state paused, pause overlay shown; Escape again → playing
sonar fired; pointer lock requested but refused by this headless context, keyboard steering fallback works

frames.shows: title card over the trench, best score, full control list, press-to-dive
live dive at ~480 m flown by the pilot with the real rules, HUD, spore trail

frames.shot: live play, 16 s of real W thrust after Enter
frames.shows: deeper water, HUD live, threat warning frame lit by a nearby drifter
result screen with outcome, score breakdown, best and R — dive again

render_cost.measured_how: renderer.info.render after a staged play frame at 1280x720
render_cost.fps_note: Not measured: requestAnimationFrame is throttled in this headless tab and gl.finish() does not prove a flush under ANGLE/SwiftShader. No fps claim is made.

legibility_measured_at_1280x720.finding: All boxes sit inside the 1280x720 viewport with no overlap or clipping. The smallest labels are 9-11 px; at 1:1 they read, but the judge's contact sheet shrinks the cover to at most 768x480 (0.6x), where 9-11 px type will not read. Queued for phase 5: raise the minimum type scale and recapture.

defects_found_and_fixed.defect: Keyboard steering was effectively inert: A/D produced ~0.02 rad/s instead of 1.6 rad/s, because a per-frame angle was multiplied by the simulation's per-second step.
defects_found_and_fixed.evidence: browser QA: yaw moved only 0.013 rad after holding A for 0.6 s
defects_found_and_fixed.fix: input.js now reports the mouse as an angle and the keys as a rate (yawRate); main.js converts the mouse angle into a rate for the frame. Re-checked in the browser: 0.8 s of A turned the skiff 1.333 rad.
defects_found_and_fixed.test: tests/run.test.mjs 'a yaw rate of one radian per second turns the skiff a radian in a second', including a 60 Hz vs 240 Hz agreement check

defects_found_and_fixed.defect: The threat warning used a 140 px inset box-shadow over the full screen, and the sonar used a fullscreen CSS bloom; with a CPU rasterizer these cost real milliseconds per frame.
defects_found_and_fixed.evidence: 1280x720 pages became unresponsive to CDP evaluation during live play; the 780x493 tab did not
defects_found_and_fixed.fix: index.html: the warning is now a 2 px coloured frame; the heavy blur/shadows are gone

open_risks: fps is unverified in this environment (no GPU); only geometry cost is known

the staged ?shot=threat mode runs up to 4 x 90 s of simulation at load and twice crashed the headless renderer; the threat frame was therefore captured from live play instead, and the mode is a candidate for removal in phase 5
smallest HUD type (9-11 px) is below comfortable size for the judge's downscaled contact sheet
